## Get the Methods Vault Workspace

### Liaison Methods Vault

Your complete VS Code course workspace for the Open Methods Hub.

You do not download a ZIP. Instead, open the template repository on GitHub, click **Use this template** to create your own copy, then clone it into VS Code.

**[🧱 Open the Methods Vault template on GitHub](https://github.com/AURA-Lab-SIUE/v2v-methods-vault){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}**

**What's Included:**
- 📁 **00_Inbox**: Quick capture area
- 📔 **01_Journal**: Weekly reflection entries
- 📚 **02_Literature**: Reading notes
- 🔬 **03_Project**: Research workspace (prospectus, codebook, data, drafts)
- 🖼️ **04_Resources**: Attachments and media
- 📋 **_templates**: The journal template (`_templates/journal-entry.md`) and other reusable starting files

For step-by-step instructions, see the [Methods Vault Setup](methods-vault-setup.qmd) guide.

## Learning Templates

Ready-to-use templates in your Methods Vault workspace:

:::{.resource-card}

#### 📔 Weekly Journal Template
<span class="resource-badge time">10-15 min</span>

Use this each week to reflect on your learning using one of three thinking paths:
- **The Connector** - How does this relate to what I know?
- **The Troubleshooter** - What problems did I solve?
- **The Critic** - Does this match my experience?

[View Template](../methods-vault.qmd){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}
:::

:::{.resource-card}

#### 📋 Data Dictionary Template
<span class="resource-badge time">15-20 min</span>

## FAQ {#faq}

**Q: Do I need to download the textbook?**  
A: No, it's optional. You can access course readings through the library or online sources.

**Q: Can I use Excel instead of R?**  
A: Yes, Excel works for basic analysis. R is recommended for more complex projects.

**Q: What if I already use a note-taking app?**
A: The Methods Vault workspace in VS Code is the recommended approach for this course, since the journal template and Foam note-linking are built around it. You can keep personal notes elsewhere, but graded work lives in the workspace.

**Q: Where do I turn in my work?**
A: Save deliverables in your Methods Vault workspace under `03_Project/`. Dr. Leith will collect via email or learning management system.

**Q: Can I work with others?**  
A: Absolutely! Pair programming and collaborative analysis are encouraged. Document who contributed what.

**Q: What if I fall behind?**  
A: Reach out to Dr. Leith early. The phases are structured but flexible—we can adjust timelines if needed.

**Q: Are there textbooks or readings?**  
A: Course readings will be posted in each phase. Check Phase 1 for the syllabus.

## Recommended Third-Party Resources

### For Data Analysis
- [R4DS Online Learning Community](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/) - Free R guide
- [Python Data Science Handbook](https://jakevdp.github.io/PythonDataScienceHandbook/) - Free Python guide
- [Kaggle Learn](https://kaggle.com/learn) - Short courses on data skills

### For Research Methods
- [JSTOR Daily](https://daily.jstor.org/) - Accessible research articles
- [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/) - Academic search
- [ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/) - Connect with researchers

### For Communication
- [Data Viz Catalogue](https://www.datavizcatalogue.com/) - Chart types and usage
- [Canva](https://www.canva.com/) - Free design templates
- [Hemingway App](http://www.hemingwayapp.com/) - Improve your writing clarity

## Software Comparison Chart

| Tool | Cost | Best For | Learning Curve |
|---|---|---|---|
| **VS Code + Foam** | Free | Note-taking, workspace organization, note-linking | Easy |
| **Git/GitHub** | Free | Version control, collaboration | Medium |
| **R** | Free | Statistical analysis, detailed control | Medium-Hard |
| **Python** | Free | Data wrangling, flexible analysis | Medium |
| **VS Code** | Free | Code editing, multiple languages | Medium |
| **Excel** | Paid | Quick analysis, pivot tables | Easy |
